finding.claim: The new @role: resolution check (and the references/*.md check) run err() inside a `grep | sort | sed | while read` pipeline subshell; FAIL=1 set there never reaches the parent shell, so detected drift exits 0 and prints 'CLEAN — no drift.' plus an unconditional 'ok: role files present, registered, @role refs resolve' line.
finding.evidence: Controlled repro (tmp copy of script, prompts/x.md containing '@role:ghostrole', all other checks passing): output 'DRIFT: @role:ghostrole referenced but agents/ghostrole.md missing' + 'CLEAN — no drift.' + EXIT CODE 0. `FAIL=0; err(){ FAIL=1; }; echo x | while read r; do err $r; done; echo $FAIL` → 0.

verdict.analysisSummary: Independently reproduced with a minimal fixture: the new @role: check prints DRIFT yet the script exits 0 and reports CLEAN. The enforcement gate (pre-commit hook + CI) silently passes on the exact drift class it was added to catch; CHANGELOG's 'Red-tested' claim could only have asserted stdout.
verdict.suggestedFix: Hoist the loop out of the pipeline (read into an array first, or use process substitution / lastpipe), make the trailing ok() conditional on the collected failures.

finding.claim: roleBody's first regex only strips a LEADING HTML comment, but every real role file (agents/worker.md, reviewer.md, scout.md, quality-reviewer.md) places the dispatch-note HTML comment AFTER the '# Role:' line, so the orchestrator-facing dispatch note is injected verbatim into every resolved subagent prompt.
finding.evidence: Live run: roleBody(fs.readFileSync('agents/worker.md','utf8')) returns a body starting with "<!-- Verbatim subagent system prompt — pasted into `prompt:` by the orchestrator.\n Dispatch policy..." — the inline comment says 'Drop leading HTML comment (the dispatch note)' and it is not dropped.

verdict.analysisSummary: Re-ran roleBody on the real agents/worker.md: the dispatch-note HTML comment survives into the substituted prompt. The code's own inline comment states the note should be dropped; the regex assumes comment-before-Role order, real files are Role-then-comment. Orchestrator-facing meta-instructions leak into every @role: subagent prompt.
verdict.suggestedFix: Strip the comment regardless of position relative to the Role header (e.g. remove the leading # Role: line first, then the leading comment), and add a test asserting the comment is gone for the real file layout.

finding.claim: Contradiction between normative docs: next.md's four dispatch templates still instruct `prompt: "<verbatim body of agents/worker.md>"` (and reviewer/scout equivalents) while agents/dispatch-shapes.md and agents/execution-doctrine.md — both marked 'Normative — follow exactly' — mandate `prompt: "@role:worker"` for the same default dispatches, and agents/registry.md declares 'Roles are referenced as @role:<name> in dispatch shapes'. next.md never mentions @role: or dispatch-shapes.md at all.
finding.evidence: grep -n 'verbatim body' prompts/next.md → lines 141/174/204/290; grep -n '@role\|dispatch-shapes' prompts/next.md → no matches; agents/dispatch-shapes.md:1-6 ('Normative — follow exactly... Role prompts use the @role:<name> convention').

verdict.analysisSummary: Verified all four '<verbatim body>' templates in prompts/next.md against the three normative docs mandating @role:. Two normative sources specify different shapes for the same default dispatch, and next.md (the most-used entry point) never points at dispatch-shapes.md. Behavioral consequence: nondeterministic orchestration style and the extension's substitution path may never fire for /next sessions following the inline template.
verdict.suggestedFix: Update next.md's four templates to prompt: '@role:<name>' with the fallback note, and reference agents/dispatch-shapes.md.

finding.claim: CHANGELOG states the extension is 'Pure logic unit-tested (13 tests, `bun test`)' but the shipped tests/extension.test.ts contains 25 tests (bun test: '25 pass').

finding.claim: missingFinalVerdicts compares done-task count against the NUMBER OF REVIEW FILES containing '**ok: true**', not per-task verdicts — ok:true files from a previous, non-archived (abandoned) plan, or a single file legitimately covering multiple tasks, mask real missing verdicts (Math.max clamps to 0).
finding.evidence: finalOkTrue = reviewFiles.filter((f) => /\*\*ok: true\*\*/.test(f.content)).length; missingFinalVerdicts = max(0, doneTasks - finalOkTrue). Reviews are only archived on SHIP (prompts/review.md:122-130); an abandoned plan leaves its ok:true files in .workflows/reviews for the next plan's watchdog to count.

verdict.analysisSummary: File-count vs task-count masking is real and reachable after an abandoned plan, but the watchdog is explicitly reminder-grade and the normal flow (per-task files, SHIP archiving) limits the window. Whether to tighten (match review files to done task ids) is a design decision.
verdict.suggestedFix: Derive finalOkTrue per done task id (reviews/<task-id>.md containing a final '**ok: true**') rather than a global file count.

finding.claim: changelogPending is derived purely from plan statuses (done === total) and never inspects CHANGELOG.md, so after /review Stage 3 writes the entry the 'plan complete — SHIP requires a CHANGELOG.md entry' line can re-fire as a false positive whenever any other drift boolean flips (state-key change re-notifies with the stale changelog part). Additionally the file header comment (and CHANGELOG) promise 'Reminds once per new gap count (no spam)' while the implementation dedupes on the boolean state ('one reminder per episode') — count changes never re-notify.
finding.evidence: computeDocsDrift: changelogPending = total > 0 && done === total — no CHANGELOG.md read anywhere in the watchdog; header comment extensions/index.ts:11-12 'Reminds once per new gap count' vs inline comment 'one reminder per episode, not per count change' vs dedupe key built from booleans only.

verdict.analysisSummary: Both behaviors verified in source (changelogPending ignores CHANGELOG.md content; dedupe is boolean-episode, not gap-count as the header/CHANGELOG claim). Each is defensible as reminder-grade; the internal doc contradiction (header vs inline comment) should be resolved by a human choosing the intended contract.
verdict.suggestedFix: Pick one dedupe contract and align header comment + CHANGELOG; optionally read CHANGELOG.md to clear changelogPending after the SHIP entry exists.
